responses.strategic_rationale: Rationale: The Bonn residential parasomnia plan sits at the intersection of rigorous physiological monitoring, participant safety, and sustainable funding. Core tensions revolve around scaling capacity vs. validated data quality, preserving privacy while enabling collaboration, and reducing manual review workload without sacrificing annotation accuracy. The six levers address these tensions by conditioning capacity expansion on pilot performance, establishing privacy-first data governance, advancing semi-automated event triage with independent validation, refining recruitment to meet milestones, building durable data infrastructure, and instituting governance that safeguards progress without paralyzing operations. Together these levers support Aim 2 longitudinal phenotyping and Aim 3 semi-automated triage within a 3-year, €3.8M budget.

levers.name: Staged expansion to 12 suites following pilot validation
levers.consequences: Expanding to 12 suites raises capture capacity and data throughput, accelerating enrollment and longitudinal measurement, but requires higher fixed costs and staffing; if pilot signals remain borderline, the additional capacity may not translate into proportional scientific gains.
options: Proceed with expansion only after pilot demonstrates data quality, manageable false alarms, and safe staffing margins.
Maintain eight suites for the study horizon, reallocating funds to analytics and personnel training instead of physical expansion.
Adopt modular renovations to allow rapid flex between eight active and potential twelve suites without major reconstruction.
levers.review_lever: Expansion to 12 suites boosts throughput and data yield, but raises fixed costs and staffing demands; if pilot signals remain borderline, the additional capacity may not translate into proportional scientific gains.

levers.name: Privacy-centric data governance for residential parasomnia data
levers.consequences: Establishing privacy-centric governance ensures compliant, de-identified datasets and controlled access, reducing institutional risk; however, it may slow external collaboration and data reuse unless governance processes are streamlined and well-justified.
options: Adopt strict de-identification, controlled-access repositories, and data-use agreements to enable de-identified datasets while preserving privacy.
Pursue early data-sharing partnerships with a formal governance charter to balance openness with privacy constraints.
Create an on-site data escrow with tiered access for investigators, auditors, and external collaborators under legal agreements.
levers.review_lever: Privacy-centric governance reduces external data access, enhances participant protection, and safeguards institutional risk, but may slow external collaboration and data reuse unless governance processes are streamlined and well-justified.

levers.name: Semi-automated event-triage tooling for parasomnia episodes
levers.consequences: Deploying semi-automated triage reduces adjudication workload and speeds initial event labeling, enabling earlier signal capture; however, reliance on automated cues risks missing atypical parasomnia presentations, requiring continuous calibration, independent validation, and alignment with the dual-human scoring standard to maintain safety.
options: Integrate a semi-automated triage system with dual-human adjudication to reduce manual review time and improve consistency.
Pilot a rule-based triage layer prioritizing high-quality events for rapid scorer review to increase throughput.
Engage external collaborators for independent validation on a subset of events to ensure generalizability across sites.
levers.review_lever: Semi-automated triage cuts reviewer workload and speeds event categorization, yet may introduce systematic misses if the model is not well-calibrated, requiring ongoing validation and careful monitoring.

levers.name: Structured recruitment funnel with pre-admission pathways
levers.consequences: Structured recruitment funnel accelerates enrollment and reduces dropouts, providing more reliable timelines for study progression, but increases upfront screening workload, coordination across multiple clinics, and ethics processing, potentially straining startup pace if staffing remains limited and timelines tighten.
options: Strengthen structured pre-admission pathway to confirm eligibility and consent before hospital contact to reduce dropouts.
Introduce matched controls recruitment incentives calibrated to per-night compensation ensuring comparability while maintaining budget limits.
Expand regional referrals through neurologists and sleep clinics with streamlined ethics approvals to accelerate enrollment.
levers.review_lever: Structured recruitment funnel accelerates enrollment and reduces dropouts, but increases upfront screening workload and coordination across clinics, potentially straining startup pace if staffing remains limited.

levers.name: Sustainable data infrastructure and storage strategy
levers.consequences: Robust storage minimizes data loss and ensures auditability across ongoing stays, while enabling reproducible analyses and compliant data sharing; however, it requires ongoing capital, maintenance, and governance, and without scale, data growth may outpace capacity, delaying results.
options: Upgrade on-site NAS with tiered backups and cloud replication to prevent data loss during extended stays.
Implement automated scoring workflow to distribute annotation workload evenly among two independent raters for consistency.
Schedule quarterly audits of data integrity and access controls to avoid compliance gaps over time.
levers.review_lever: Robust storage minimizes data loss and ensures auditability across ongoing stays, while enabling reproducible analyses and compliant data sharing; however, it requires ongoing capital, maintenance, and governance, and without scale, data growth may outpace capacity, delaying results.

levers.name: External scientific advisory governance cadence
levers.consequences: External oversight improves accountability, milestone tracking, and risk management through independent review, providing resilience against scope creep and data quality issues; however, it introduces slower decision cycles, potential misalignment with urgent operational needs, and additional administrative overhead that could delay execution if not managed.
options: Institutionalize biannual external board reviews to adjust milestones and budget allocations based on progress and risk.
Define explicit failure triggers with external audit and formal remediation plan to restore compliance when necessary.
Preserve PI operational authority while enabling budget reallocations above €50K with board consent to navigate risks.
levers.review_lever: External oversight improves accountability and milestone tracking, but introduces slower decision cycles and possible misalignment with rapid operational needs.

responses.strategic_rationale: The Bonn residential parasomnia unit must balance safe, privacy-conscious in-person data collection with achieving adequate event yield for longitudinal phenotyping and method validation within €3.8M over 3 years. Core tensions include capacity versus utilization, high-cost PSG nights versus scalable low-burden monitoring, recruitment throughput versus data quality, and open dissemination versus governance complexity with industry partners. The six levers target: phased capacity scaling anchored to data quality; sensor and scheduling optimization to maximize signal while controlling cost; recruitment refinement to maintain enrollment momentum; governance of data sharing and publications to attract funding without eroding scientific independence; adaptable staffing to match workload; and structured industry collaboration that preserves core academic rights.

levers.name: Phased capacity scaling tied to data-quality milestones
levers.consequences: Expanding to 10 suites increases fixed costs and staffing beyond the current 8-suites baseline; downstream, higher event capture improves statistical power for Aim 2 and publications, but raises false-alarm burden and safety-management workload if utilization remains uneven.
options: Scale to 10 suites after achieving predefined data-quality thresholds and acceptable false-alarm rate in the pilot cohort.
Maintain 8 suites but extend visit windows and analysis slots to capture more events per participant.
Pause expansion until independent external review validates patient throughput, data quality, and staffing sufficiency for scale.
levers.review_lever: Expanding to 10 suites aligns with data-power goals but risks overstretching staffing and safety oversight unless pilot-driven utilization proves consistent.

levers.name: Sensor-suite orchestration for data yield
levers.consequences: Adopting adaptive sensing schedules prioritizes enhanced PSG nights after flagged events, improving data quality and event characterization; downstream, this concentrates high-cost resources during rare events, risking delays in enrollment and potential participant drop-out if scheduling becomes complex.
options: Adopt adaptive sensing with automated PSG nights triggered by initial-night flags to improve early-event capture.
Maintain consistent low-burden monitoring across all participants to minimize per-participant costs and execution complexity during recruitment.
Implement staged escalation nights for all participants regardless of flag to standardize data quality and comparability across sites.
levers.review_lever: Adaptive sensing offers data gains but concentrates expensive PSG resources during rare events, risking uneven data quality and participant dissatisfaction if nocturnal patterns are highly variable.

levers.name: Pre-admission vetting intensification with collateral-history integration
levers.consequences: Intensifying pre-admission vetting improves expected event yield per enrolled participant but raises screening overhead and could slow overall enrollment, challenging the pace and timeline flexibility.
options: Increase collateral-history verification and pre-screening interviews to improve eligibility accuracy and predict event yield per admission.
Broaden referral networks to include regional neurologists and sleep clinics with streamlined consent workflows and faster enrollment.
Offer flexible admission slots and weekend visits to reduce dropouts and align with participant availability.
levers.review_lever: More stringent pre-screening improves yield on paper yet may throttle recruitment pace and exclude borderline cases that could contribute meaningful data, slowing timeline flexibility.

levers.name: Public data access framework for de-identified physiological data
levers.consequences: Establishing a formal framework to deposit de-identified physiological data in a recognized repository; downstream, this broadens collaboration and publication potential, but increases governance overhead and demands strict data-use agreements to prevent misuse.
options: Publish synthetic or aggregated subsets first to balance openness with privacy constraints while enabling early collaboration.
Release controlled-access de-identified datasets via a recognized repository, supported by explicit data-use agreements and reviewer-based access controls.
Establish a staged data-release calendar synchronized with publication milestones to manage expectations and privacy risk.
levers.review_lever: Publishing de-identified data broadens impact but increases governance friction and potential delays; efficient DUAs are essential to avoid bottlenecks while preserving privacy.

levers.name: Staffing model responsive to event-triage workload
levers.consequences: Shifting staffing to align with nights showing higher event density reduces response delays and improves data quality; downstream, it increases overtime costs and scheduling complexity during peak periods, potentially straining budget lines if event yield fluctuates beyond projections.
options: Implement flexible nurse-technician assignments across the eight suites to cover peak-hour event triage and scoring.
Consolidate overnight coverage into a core team with surge capacity allocated by event queues to optimize throughput.
Pilot cross-training enabling technicians to perform preliminary scoring during high-volume nights without compromising safety and response times.
levers.review_lever: Flexible staffing improves responsiveness and data quality during peak nights but introduces overtime risk and budget volatility if event yield deviates from projections.

levers.name: Partnership governance for external collaborators and publication control
levers.consequences: Formalizing industry collaboration terms preserves publication rights and sets pre-publication comment windows; downstream, this enables conditional funding and technology transfer opportunities, but increases precedence for negotiation, potentially delaying manuscript submission timelines if milestones slip.
options: Negotiate milestone-based funding with transparent publication rights to align incentives and maintain open-access dissemination for all primary outcomes.
Require pre-agreed data-use and authorship terms with any external partner prior to data sharing and joint manuscript preparation.
Limit industry access to de-identified aggregates while preserving collaboration through joint methodology papers and shared conference presentations.
levers.review_lever: Structured collaboration terms sustain publication rights and funding while potentially delaying outputs; early, explicit milestones and clear review timelines can mitigate negotiation drag.

responses.strategic_rationale: The Bonn parasomnia program navigates core tensions among data fidelity, participant burden, privacy, recruitment velocity, and safety governance. The six levers balance depth of physiological data against naturalistic environments, privacy protections with external collaboration, rapid enrollment with retention costs, mature event-triage fidelity with cross-site generalizability, scalable storage with operational practicality, and rigorous safety oversight that does not impede iterative protocol improvements.

levers.name: Naturalistic-first monitoring protocol
levers.consequences: Emphasizes naturalistic data capture with minimal participant burden, enabling higher enrollment and longer stay windows. However, the reduced PSG coverage increases reliance on automated triage, potentially elevating risk of missed parasomnia events if algorithm sensitivity is insufficient; necessitates rigorous validation and redundant human reviews.
options: Use nightly low-burden surveillance (dry EEG, mattress sensors, cameras) for all participants, reserving full PSG escalation on flagged events.
Carry fixed PSG on every night for every participant to standardize event validation and scoring.
Randomly rotate cohorts through enhanced nights early to calibrate scoring consistency before large-scale deployment protocols.
levers.review_lever: Naturalistic-first monitoring reduces intrusiveness and may improve participant retention, but heavy reliance on automation raises the risk of missed events if triage sensitivity is inadequate, requiring rigorous validation and rapid manual review pathways.

levers.name: Data governance with tiered access and consent-driven sharing
levers.consequences: Privacy controls guard participant dignity and institutional compliance, but they can introduce data silos, gatekeeping delays, and slower collaboration with external groups; balancing access must avoid stalling useful cross-site analyses and timely method validation.
options: Apply strict de-identification on video streams and limit access to the core data team with formal access logs.
Implement tiered access with time-bound embargoes for video data and role-based permissions across projects to ensure compliance.
Enable controlled, consent-driven external data-sharing via formal data-use agreements and annual privacy-assurance reviews to maintain compliance.
levers.review_lever: Stricter data governance safeguards privacy but may impede timely data sharing and external collaboration; the need for multi-tier access processes could slow rapid replication.

levers.name: Retention-focused recruitment and scheduling optimization
levers.consequences: Improved enrollment pace and reduced withdrawal risk come with higher compensation and expanded screening costs, straining the budget; without scalable funding gains in throughput, long-stay economics may limit scalability and require tighter stay caps.
options: Offer elevated per-night compensation and enhanced meals to boost enrollment pace and participant retention during long stays.
Implement pre-admission collateral-history verification to reduce late withdrawals and align eligibility earlier during screening and improve conversion to randomization.
Expand referral networks regionally and schedule flexible pre-screening slots to minimize appointment delays and increase screening throughput significantly.
levers.review_lever: Retention strategies raise enrollment and retention but increase budget pressure; extended stays may complicate staffing models and limit scalability unless funding and planning keep pace.

levers.name: Event-triage maturity and cross-site validation
levers.consequences: Advancing triage maturity improves consistency across scorers, but it increases coordination overhead and inter-site alignment complexity; if not carefully managed, throughput may slow while generalizability to Bonn's population remains uncertain.
options: Institute cross-site scoring audits to harmonize event adjudication and reduce inter-rater variance across sites and timelines.
Adopt adaptive sensitivity in the triage algorithm based on current event density and occupancy levels.
Publish reproducible benchmarking datasets and scorecards to enable external replication and external validation by independent groups.
levers.review_lever: Cross-site triage maturity improves consistency but adds coordination overhead; overfitting scoring to initial sites risks reduced generalizability across Bonn's population and schedules.

levers.name: Storage and data integrity infrastructure expansion
levers.consequences: Scaling storage and enforcing encryption reduces data-loss risk and supports long-term replication, yet adds operational overhead, longer data-processing cycles, and higher maintenance costs; real-time access for urgent decision-making may be constrained unless indexing and caching are optimized.
options: Scale EEG-BIDS compliant storage with encrypted backups to university storage, ensuring regulatory readiness for phase-two proposals.
Implement real-time sensor-health dashboards and automated alerting for data loss and hardware faults to prevent unnoticed gaps.
Plan modular NAS expansion aligned with pilot milestones to prevent capacity bottlenecks during growth phases.
levers.review_lever: Data-storage expansion reduces loss risk but heightens operational complexity and cost; encryption and offsite backups may slow real-time access for urgent decision-making.

levers.name: Safety governance and regulatory alignment for extended stays
levers.consequences: Safety governance anchors compliant operations during extended stays, yet frequent audits may slow protocol evolution and stifle iterative improvements; achieving balance requires pre-approved change pathways and risk-based review tempo to sustain safety without choking innovation.
options: Institute quarterly safety drills and hazard-risk reviews to maintain compliant operations during peak occupancy periods.
Dynamic staffing model adjusts night coverage based on observed event rate and patient flow to maintain safety.
Engage external IRB liaison to accelerate amendments triggered by pilot data while preserving rigor and compliance.
levers.review_lever: Safety governance reinforces compliance but excessive audits could slow protocol evolution; balancing flexibility with oversight requires pre-approved change pathways to avoid operational disruption.

system_prompt:
You are an expert strategic analyst. Generate solution space parameters following these directives:

1. **Output Requirements**
   - You must generate 5 to 7 levers per response.
   - Each lever's `options` field must contain exactly 3 qualitative strategic choices as plain strings.

2. **Lever Quality Standards**
   - Consequences: describe the direct effect of pulling this lever, then at least one downstream implication or trade-off. Be concise and grounded — only cite numbers the project context provides directly. Target length: 30–60 words.
   - Options MUST:
     • Represent genuinely distinct strategic pathways (not just labels)
     • Include at least one unconventional or non-obvious approach
     • NO prefixes (e.g., "Option A:", "Choice 1:")

3. **Strategic Framing**
   - Name each lever using language drawn directly from the project's own domain — avoid formulaic patterns or repeated prefixes
   - Frame options as complete strategic approaches
   - Ensure levers challenge core project assumptions

4. **Validation Protocols**
   - For `review_lever`:
     A one-sentence critical review (20–40 words). Examples:
     - "Switching from seasonal contract labor to year-round employees stabilizes harvest quality, but the idle-wage burden during the 5-month off-season adds a fixed cost that erases the per-unit savings unless utilization reaches year-round levels."
     - "Each additional clinical site requires its own IRB approval, site-initiation visit, and staff credentialing — a sequential overhead that compounds rather than parallelizes, so doubling site count does not halve enrollment time."
     - "Pooling catastrophe risk across three coastal regions reduces expected annual loss on paper, but a single regional hurricane season can correlate all three simultaneously, turning the diversification assumption into a concentration risk at the worst possible moment."
     Do not use square brackets or placeholder text.

5. **Prohibitions**
   - NO prefixes/labels in options (e.g., "Option A:", "Choice 1:")
   - NO generic option labels (e.g., "Optimize X", "Tolerate Y")
   - NO placeholder consequences or bracket-wrapped templates
   - NO fabricated statistics or percentages without evidence from the project context
   - NO marketing language (e.g., "game-changing", "cutting-edge", "revolutionary")

6. **Length Limits**
   - Keep each `review_lever` to 20–40 words.
   - Each option: 15–25 words, a concrete actionable approach with an action verb.
   - Maintain parallel grammatical structure across options
   - Ensure options are self-contained descriptions
user_prompt:
File 'plan.txt':
Plan:
Establish a 3-year residential longitudinal research unit in Bonn, Germany, for the study of adult NREM parasomnias — sleepwalking, confusional arousals, and sleep terrors — with a secondary exploratory arm for REM sleep behavior disorder under a separate protocol with dedicated neurologic screening, reflecting RBD's distinct clinical trajectory per current AASM guidance. The facility is affiliated with University Hospital Bonn's Department of Epileptology, leveraging its existing long-term video-EEG monitoring culture, and addresses a specific methodological gap: traditional single-night polysomnography rarely captures infrequent parasomnia events, while outpatient actigraphy lacks physiological resolution. The unit houses 8 active sleep suites at launch in a converted residential property in a quiet Bonn neighborhood, renovated for safety (padded corridor edges, restricted-opening windows, silent exterior door alarms, fire safety, acoustic treatment, network cabling, accessibility modifications) while preserving a domestic feel — if the environment is too clinical, naturalistic behavior is suppressed. Physical capacity exists for 12 suites, but expansion is deferred until the pilot proves acceptable data quality, manageable false alarm rates, safe staffing ratios, and usable annotation throughput. Sensing uses a tiered acquisition model: nightly low-burden monitoring via dry-electrode EEG headbands, contact-free mattress sensors, unobtrusively mounted infrared cameras, ambient microphones, and environmental sensors; scheduled enhanced nights with fuller PSG montage including standard scalp EEG, EOG, chin EMG, and leg EMG on the first night, one mid-stay night, and the final night per participant; and escalation nights deploying full PSG after technician-flagged events to capture recurrence at clinical-grade resolution. All streams are time-synchronized and stored in EEG-BIDS-compatible format on a local NAS with nightly encrypted backup to university storage, annotated in real time by the night technician and later scored by two independent raters using AASM criteria with inter-rater reliability reported. Public data sharing is limited to de-identified physiological and sensor data under data use agreements — bedroom video carries severe privacy constraints and is not deposited in public repositories. The scientific program has three explicit aims: Aim 1, establish and operationally validate the residential capture model as safe, ethics-approved, and sustainable; Aim 2, characterize within-person and between-person parasomnia patterns longitudinally, including episode frequency, morphology, triggers, and temporal clustering; Aim 3, develop and benchmark semi-automated event-triage tools that rank probable parasomnia episodes and reduce manual review burden, evaluated against dual human scorer agreement rather than promising autonomous diagnosis.

Participant recruitment targets adults aged 18–65 with NREM parasomnia confirmed through a structured pre-admission pathway: specialist clinical interview, collateral history from bed partner or household member where available, prior or screening polysomnography, and a structured exclusion checklist adjudicated by the PI. Explicit exclusions are nocturnal epilepsy or suspected epilepsy mimics, untreated obstructive sleep apnea, active major substance use disorder, severe psychiatric instability, and wandering or injury risk beyond facility capability. Recruitment channels are the University Hospital Bonn sleep clinic, regional neurologist referrals, and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Schlafforschung und Schlafmedizin network, with per-night compensation of €80 plus meals. A matched control group provides baseline nocturnal movement, arousal patterns, and false-positive sensor activity under identical residential monitoring conditions, enabling benchmarking of the event-triage tools against normal nocturnal behavior. Event-yield planning assumes that based on the inclusion criterion of at least 2 self-reported episodes per month, approximately 70–80% of admitted participants will produce at least one captured and adjudicated event during a 2–8 week stay; stays may be extended up to 2 additional weeks for participants with zero captured events after the initial period, capped at 10 weeks total, with a protocol ceiling of 20% unproductive admissions before triggering a recruitment-criteria review. The core team is 9 people: a PI who is a board-certified sleep medicine physician, 2 postdoctoral researchers in sleep neurophysiology and computational neuroscience respectively, 3 research technicians rotating night shifts to ensure safe coverage of 8 active suites with adequate margin for event response and annotation, a clinical psychologist specializing in sleep disorders, a data engineer managing the sensor pipeline, and a study coordinator handling recruitment, consent, scheduling, and ethics compliance.

Budget is €3.8 million over 3 years, gated: €1.8M year one covering property lease and renovation at approximately €750K, equipment at approximately €450K, staff hiring accounting for German social insurance contributions and actual overnight coverage, ethics approval, and a pilot cohort of 15–20 participants; €1.2M year two covering full operations with 30–35 participants, the enhanced-night PSG program, first publications, and event-triage algorithm development; €800K year three conditional on demonstrable progress by month 24. Personnel costs are approximately €2M over three years and remaining funds cover participant compensation, independent scoring time, data storage and retention, regulatory and legal work, and contingency. Funding sources are DFG research grant and University of Bonn internal research funding as the primary pillars, with a pharmaceutical industry partnership as optional upside rather than a feasibility requirement — if secured, the academic team retains full publication rights with the pharma partner receiving a 30-day pre-publication comment window only. Success criteria at 36 months: safe residential monitoring operations sustained for at least 24 months, enrollment of 50–70 NREM parasomnia participants plus matched controls, capture of a prespecified minimum number of independently adjudicated parasomnia events sufficient for Aim 2 phenotyping analysis, 2–3 peer-reviewed publications in sleep medicine journals covering methods validation and longitudinal characterization, a benchmarked semi-automated event-triage model with reported sensitivity, specificity, and agreement against dual human scoring, de-identified physiological dataset deposited in a recognized repository, and a submitted phase-two grant proposal for expansion and intervention studies. Failure triggers: if by month 18 the facility has enrolled fewer than 25 participants or captured fewer than 40 adjudicated events, the program undergoes external review. Governance is a 3-member external scientific advisory board reviewing progress every 6 months, with the PI holding operational authority and budget reallocations above €50K requiring board approval. Banned words: AI, blockchain, app, VR, AR, gamification, wearable startup, consumer product, DAO, NFT, metaverse, smart home, autonomous diagnosis, digital therapeutic, SaaS, marketplace, validated (in the context of claiming a mature deployable system). Pick a realistic scenario — this is an early-stage clinical research facility producing methods validation and phenotyping work, not a finished diagnostic platform.
